---
title: QA accounts
description: Issue disposable Tuturuuu and Meet accounts and browser sessions from the CLI.
---

The QA CLI uses the existing [QA test user operator](/build/development-tools/qa-test-users)
and its root workspace permission. Each issue or session command creates a
fresh QA identity and isolated workspace. The initial identity owns that QA
workspace. Use the legacy run workflow to add participants to the same space.

```sh
ttr qa account issue --product tuturuuu --role member --ttl 2h --workspace qa --json
ttr qa session --product meet --role member --out ./storageState.json --json
ttr qa list
ttr qa cleanup
```

The CLI writes credentials and Playwright state to owner-only files. Use a
private output directory. Both products share the same operator ledger.
Cleanup acts on expired identities. To recover a failed session command,
use the reported run and user IDs with the legacy session and cleanup commands.

The product commands currently support the member role on Tuturuuu and Meet.

## Upskii disposable fixtures

```sh
ttr qa account issue --product upskii --role teacher --json
ttr qa session --product upskii --role student --out ./storageState.json --json
```

Run on the authorized macOS executor with the Upskii provisioner Keychain
entry. Each command creates one two-hour test identity. Session issuance uses
normal password sign-in and verifies the exact user ID and email before storing
the browser cookie. The task can enroll this identity in a synthetic class using
the normal invitation flow. Accounts expire on the server. If issuance fails
after contacting the provisioner, reconcile the reported request ID before
issuing a replacement.

Tuturuuu's unattended CI uses a workflow-bound GitHub OIDC token. The QA CLI
does not read the reported M4 Tuturuuu fleet-smoke Keychain item because the
documented QA endpoint has no authentication contract for that item.
